subject: Architecture
title: The I-35W Mississippi Bridge: Wake-Up Call
description: A 60-second lesson on The I-35W Mississippi Bridge: Wake-Up Call.

hook.text: On August 1, 2007, a busy Minneapolis highway bridge collapsed during rush hour, killing 13 people.

buildup.text: The I-35W bridge had been rated 'structurally deficient' for 17 years before it failed.

discovery.text: Gusset plates — thin steel connectors — were half as thick as they should have been. A design error from 1967.

twist.text: Heavy construction equipment on the deck at the time of collapse added extra load to already weak connections.

climax.text: The U.S. government allocated $1.7 billion for bridge repairs. Over 70,000 bridges were still rated deficient.

punchline.text: We knew it was failing. We just didn't fix it in time.

quiz.question: What design flaw caused the I-35W bridge collapse?
options: The foundations were built on unstable sand
Gusset plates were half as thick as they should have been
The suspension cables corroded from road salt

details.summary: The I-35W Mississippi River bridge in Minneapolis collapsed during rush hour on August 1, 2007, killing 13 people. A steel gusset plate just 12.7mm thick — undersized in the original 1967 design — failed under the added weight of construction materials and traffic.
details.whyItMatters: The I-35W collapse revealed that thousands of bridges across America had been rated structurally deficient for years without adequate funding for repair. It forced a national conversation about infrastructure investment that continues today.
takeaways: Collapsed during rush hour on August 1, 2007, killing 13 people
An undersized gusset plate from the original 1967 design failed
It exposed widespread neglect of aging US bridge infrastructure

faq.question: What is a gusset plate?
faq.answer: Gusset plates are flat steel plates that connect multiple truss members at a single point, like a hub connecting spokes. The I-35W bridge's gusset plates were too thin for the loads they carried — a design error hidden for 40 years until the added weight of construction materials triggered failure.

faq.question: How many US bridges are structurally deficient?
faq.answer: As of recent reports, over 42,000 US bridges are rated structurally deficient (about 7% of the total). The 2021 Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act allocated $40 billion for bridge repair — the largest dedicated bridge investment in US history.
